title: Create real time memory allocation and denormal audit tests
description:
Create a juce::UnitTest that audits processBlock for real-time safety: zero heap allocation during processing and correct denormal flushing.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/PluginProcessor.h and Source/PluginProcessor.cpp (integrated processBlock from task f.1; prepareToPlay buffer allocation and the ScopedNoDenormals guard)
- CMakeLists.txt (how existing UnitTest sources and the CTest console-runner target are registered; the ShredBoost target definition)
- Any existing tests/*.cpp using juce::UnitTest for the established pattern (registration, runner wiring)

Implementation requirements:
1. Add tests/ProcessBlockRealtimeTests.cpp defining a juce::UnitTest subclass registered with the existing console runner (no third-party testing frameworks).
2. Allocation audit: call prepareToPlay with a fixed max block size, then install a global new/delete allocation counter (e.g. override operator new/delete or a scoped allocation guard) around repeated processBlock calls; assert the allocation count is zero during processBlock.
3. Denormal audit: feed a buffer whose samples decay into the denormal range and assert that outputs are flushed to zero (denormals not present), confirming ScopedNoDenormals behavior.
4. Register tests/ProcessBlockRealtimeTests.cpp in CMakeLists.txt so it builds into the UnitTest runner and is discoverable by CTest.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: tests/ProcessBlockRealtimeTests.cpp defines a juce::UnitTest subclass and uses no third-party testing framework
The test asserts zero heap allocations occur during processBlock via an allocation counter around processBlock calls
The test asserts denormal inputs are flushed to zero in processBlock output
CMakeLists.txt registers tests/ProcessBlockRealtimeTests.cpp in the UnitTest console-runner target
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure runs the ProcessBlockRealtime test and it passes
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified

allowed: choose the allocation-counting mechanism (scoped operator new/delete override or guard)
